Why it fails the frozen task/service contract: (1) Every transmitted frame carries kind 0x06 only (hex payloads e.g. 0004 25d4 … 00000601 e7e7) with a boolean state = (rms > 0.05); records show kind "periodic_snapshot" exclusively. task.service.scope requires "Every individual start/stop plus continuous keepalive", and event_time_basis is "Confirmation time, not raw rising/falling edge". No start/stop/keepalive record is ever produced, so the required service message set is structurally absent. (2) Timing: with start_continuous_s=3 and rms_waveform's 0.08 g segment starting at 4200, the confirmation instant is 4203; event_delivery_s=10 requires delivery by 4213. The 60 s grid samples 4192.07 (0.005 g) then 4252.07 (0.08 g), and the first high-carrying frame is received at 4252.07 — ~39 s late, and event_time_error_s=1 is unachievable because the ZOH interval (4192,4252] is unobserved until 4252. Same lateness at 7852/11452/16852 and for stops (low from 4500 confirmed 4560, first low frame 4552.07 with only ~8 s to spare, and at 16920 the 120 s active interval is bracketed only by 16852/16912). (3) The 16800–16920 active interval and the four 0.08 g segments cannot be individually declared or keepalive-covered as confirmed active state by thresholded snapshots; the program is explicitly "A-style periodic snapshots and immediate FIFO upload; no start/stop confirmation state machine" per the assigned frozen control.

Retained limits: no truth/service-acceptance label is produced by the tool; models are the assumed ideal A/R chain with PROPOSED_IDEAL_DIGITAL_NOT_CALIBRATED components and physical_qualification UNKNOWN (no calibrated PV/PMIC/RMS hardware). Energy/queue feasibility in this observation does not override the missing service message and timing semantics; the result is a design-scope FAIL, not a hardware claim.
